subject: general
question: __________are in Madhya Pradesh.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bagh caves.**__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bagh Caves** is situated among the southern slopes of the Vindhyas in Bagh town of Dhar district in **Madhya Pradesh state in central India.**
 
• The Bagh Caves are a group of nine rock-cut monuments, great examples of Indian rock-cut architecture.
 
• They are believed to been built during the 5th-7th century, carved during the Satvahana dynasty. The Archaeological Survey of India has restored the place for over 17 years.
 
• These caves belong to the Buddhist faith and it is not certain, how and when these caves began to be called Bagh Gupha.
 
• The most beautiful paintings known to be created by prehistoric man can be found in these rock-cut caverns. Only 5 of the original 9 caverns have survived.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bhaja caves are a group o**f 22 rock-cut caves** located in the city of Pune, India. The caves are 400ft above the village of Bhaja. This cave belongs to the Early Buddhist schools in Maharashtra.
 
• **Kanheri caves** are a group of caves and rock-cut monuments, in the forests of The Sanjay Gandhi National Park, on the western outskirts of Mumbai, India. They contain Buddhist sculptures, carvings, paintings, and inscriptions.
 
• **Ajanta caves** are 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra state in India. The caves include paintings and rock-cut sculptures described as among the finest examples of ancient Indian art, particularly expressive paintings that present emotions through gesture, pose, and form.
